headline: Overtime paid the bill. Miami collects the first road invoice.
dek: A 33-30 grind over Indianapolis finally married Kenneth Walker III's 117 to Patrick Mahomes' 382-yard night; Sunday noon in Miami is the 3-0 chase, and Steve Spagnuolo's unit has already treated 30 points as a problem, not a footnote.
videoHook: Two-and-oh, 523 yards, zero turnovers — and a defense that already said last Sunday was too loud. Miami is not a bye just because it's noon on CBS.
theEdge: A 10.5-point road favorite on a 45.5 total (DraftKings) with an 85.3 percent ESPN FPI nod still sits at 7.6 percent to win the Super Bowl on Polymarket — the market likes Sunday in Miami more than it likes the long-term ticket, and the 30-point Colts tape is why.

storyline.lede: Kansas City is 2-0 because Eric Bieniemy's offense finally has two answers, not one. Week 1 was Walker and the clock against Denver. Week 2 was Mahomes, Travis Kelce, and 523 yards in a 33-30 overtime win over Indianapolis at Arrowhead. That is a complete enough identity to travel. It is not clean enough to treat a winless Miami team like a scheduled bye on the first road Sunday of 2026.
body: The Colts tape is the first real self-scout of the Andy Reid-Bieniemy-Spagnuolo year. Kansas City owned the math — 29 first downs, 37:00 of possession, zero turnovers, 152 on the ground after 220 in Week 1 — and still needed overtime because Indianapolis posted 24 first downs, 329 yards, and 30 points. Nick Bolton leading the club with 13 tackles is production; it is also a tell that the defense spent too much of Sunday night in a chase. Spagnuolo has already said that part out loud.

What changed from the opener is the pass. Mahomes went 32-of-47 for 382 yards and three scores, Kelce put up 9-101-1, and the red-zone finishes were Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals from the 1 after a 13-yard Kelce strike. Rashee Rice's explosive was not a random dart; it was the payoff of a look Indianapolis had already seen in Week 1. Defenses are loading for Walker, and Mahomes can see it. That is the leverage for Miami, not a reason to shelve the run.

Now the calendar gets honest. This is the first road trip, a noon CBS kick, and the front of a three-game AFC stretch that goes to Las Vegas in Week 4 and back home against the Chargers in Week 6. Kansas City is chasing 3-0 with the Raiders as the other unbeaten in the AFC West. The books have the Chiefs as a double-digit favorite. The prediction markets have not crowned anybody. The assignment is to play the Dolphins like a team that just allowed 30, not like a team that just found 523.

lastGameReview.label: Week 2 · Sun, Sep 20 · 7:20 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: On NBC at Arrowhead, Kansas City outgained Indianapolis 523-329, ran 37:00, and did not turn it over, yet still needed overtime to close a 33-30 win. Daniel Jones hit Tyler Warren from a yard out to open the night, Jonathan Taylor ripped a 24-yard touchdown just before half, and the Colts kicked two second-quarter field goals; Mahomes answered with touchdowns to Kelce, Worthy, and Royals, Walker carried 24 times for 117, and Harrison Butker's 46-yarder kept the first quarter from getting away.
analysis: The offensive story is complementarity, not a box-score spike. After Denver ate 220 rush yards, Indianapolis had to honor the inside zone, and Bieniemy cashed the other side of that respect: Mahomes at 382 yards on 47 attempts, Kelce as the chain-mover (9-101-1), and two different wideouts finishing from the 1. That is how you post 29 first downs. It is also how you survive a 5-of-13 night on third down — volume and explosives covering a conversion rate that will not travel if it stays there.

The run was not a decoy. Walker's 24-117 kept the game in under-center and play-action language even while the pass stacked 371 net yards. When the Colts loaded for the downhill game they had just watched on the Denver tape, Mahomes had the answers in the intermediate middle and on the goal line. The 13-yard Kelce score and the two 1-yard throws are the red-zone correction from a preseason that kept settling for kicks.

The defensive story is the one Spagnuolo will put on the projector. Thirty points, 24 first downs, 119 rush yards, and a 24-yard Taylor touchdown are not a fluke of finishing; they are a unit that let Indianapolis stay on schedule for 33:00. Bolton's 13 tackles mean the second level was busy. Busy is not the same as tight. A 5-of-12 Colts third-down night kept it from becoming a track meet, but the explosives and the goal-line leak to Warren are the clips that do not belong on a 2-0 tape if this defense wants to look like itself in October.

Overtime does not make it a lucky win so much as a loud one. Kansas City never trailed the turnover margin, won the yardage by almost 200, and still had to finish extra football because the points allowed outran the points earned for too long. That is the difference between a complete offense and a complete team. Miami is the first place that difference shows up on the road.

takeaways.title: The pass finally paid the run's tab
takeaways.body: Walker still got 24 carries and 117 yards, but Mahomes' 32-of-47, 382, and three scores are the new problem for coordinators. Kelce at 9-101-1 is the coverage magnet that makes Worthy's and Royals' 1-yard finishes possible.

takeaways.title: Third down is the hidden leak on a 523-yard night
takeaways.body: Five of 13 is not how a 29-first-down offense should live. Explosives and red-zone throws covered it against Indianapolis. A noon road kick will not, not if Miami can force the Chiefs into obvious passing downs.

takeaways.title: Spagnuolo already graded the defense honestly
takeaways.body: Thirty points, 329 yards, and 24 first downs are not a footnote to 2-0. Bolton leading the team in tackles is the second-level alarm. The self-scout is the actual Week 3 install.

whatWorked: Walker remaining a 24-carry feature after the Denver tape, not a change-of-pace afterthought
Mahomes-to-Kelce as the intermediate answer once Indianapolis loaded the box
Red-zone throws to Worthy and Royals from the 1 instead of another field-goal night
Zero turnovers and 37:00 of possession as the floor, even in overtime
Harrison Butker's 46-yarder answering the opening Warren touchdown so the game never tilted early
whatDidnt: The defense allowing 30 points, 24 first downs, and a 24-yard Taylor touchdown
Too many tackles for Bolton, a sign the second level was reacting instead of dictating
Letting Indianapolis hold the ball for 33:00 in a game Kansas City otherwise dominated on paper

currentState.lede: The Chiefs are 2-0 with a complete offensive menu and an incomplete defensive standard. They can lean on Walker or let Mahomes throw for 380. They cannot take a winless Miami team lightly on the first road Sunday of the year, not after Spagnuolo's own unit admitted Week 2 was too loud, and not with Chamarri Conner still easing back into the secondary.

workOn.title: Third-down offense
workOn.body: Five of 13 against Indianapolis is the first number Bieniemy has to fix before a noon kick. Mesh, boots, and easy throws have to replace hoping the next explosive covers a stalled series.

workOn.title: Points allowed, not just yards allowed
workOn.body: Indianapolis left with 30 and 24 first downs. Miami does not have to be good to make that a problem if Kansas City's defense again plays on its heels for 33 minutes.

workOn.title: Road situational football
workOn.body: This is the first true road environment of 2026. Early-down runs, clock, and a clean pocket for Mahomes matter more at noon in South Florida than they did under the lights at Arrowhead.

workOn.title: Secondary communication with Conner ramping up
workOn.body: Conner is easing back at the right time, but a returning safety cannot be asked to erase a 30-point tape by himself. Nohl Williams and the corners need a simpler Sunday than isolated man all afternoon.

thinkAbout.title: Is Miami actually a trap?
thinkAbout.body: The 2-0 club is a double-digit favorite against a winless team widely treated as the league's floor. That is exactly how noon road games get sloppy if the Colts film session stays in the building.

thinkAbout.title: How much run is enough now that the pass cashed
thinkAbout.body: Mahomes can see defenses respecting Walker. The temptation is to throw it 47 times again. The smarter 3-0 path is still 20-plus Walker carries that buy the boots and play-action.

thinkAbout.title: What 3-0 is worth in September
thinkAbout.body: Kansas City is one of eight 2-0 teams and one of two unbeaten in the AFC West with Las Vegas. A 3-0 start is a mark, not a coronation — Polymarket still has the Chiefs at 7.6 percent to win it all.

thinkAbout.title: Noise versus next snap
thinkAbout.body: Tyreek Hill reunion talk will follow this roster until it doesn't. Sunday is about Conner's snap count, Felix Anudike-Uzomah's quad, and whether Spagnuolo's calls look like the self-scout.

gamePlan.lede: First road trip of 2026, noon CBS, a winless Miami team Kansas City has beaten in five straight meetings — and a Chiefs defense that just allowed 30. The assignment is to play the Dolphins like the Colts tape, not like the spread.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City brings a two-headed offense (Walker downhill, Mahomes and Kelce when the box loads) into a building that will try to make this a speed-and-explosives problem. Miami's path is chaos and cheap points; Kansas City's path is 37-minute football, early-down runs, and a Spagnuolo plan that takes away the deep shot instead of chasing 24 first downs. Conner easing back and FAU popping up with a quad tilt the Chiefs toward simulated pressure and two-deep structure rather than a pin-the-ears-back road game.

keys.title: Run it until Miami's safeties step up, then boot
keys.body: Walker at 24-117 is the lever. Inside zone on early downs, then under-center play-action boots for Mahomes and Kelce once the box is heavy. That is how you keep a noon road game from turning into a track meet.

keys.title: Third down cannot be a 5-of-13 sequel
keys.body: Script mesh and easy throws for Kelce against man, and do not let 47 dropbacks become the plan. If Kansas City stays on schedule, Miami's best hope (chaos, explosives, a short field) never arrives.

keys.title: Spagnuolo's self-scout is the real install
keys.body: Two-deep shells to take away the shot, rally with Bolton, and mix zone blitz so a banged-up edge does not have to win every snap. Thirty points against Indianapolis is the look you take away, not the look you repeat.

keys.title: Get Conner on the field without asking him to be the entire answer
keys.body: His return is timed for the perimeter stress of a road secondary. Pair him with Nohl Williams in a simpler coverage menu. Do not isolate a ramping safety and then wonder why the Colts tape came with you on the plane.

script: Open 11/12 personnel under center: Walker inside zone, two-high look be damned, and make Miami's linebackers play downhill on snap one.
Second series: same run fake, Mahomes boot, Kelce leaking — cash the respect the Colts already showed after Denver's 220.
Keep Rice and Worthy on vertical stems off play-action so the first 20-plus of the day is scheduled, not hoped for.
Third-and-medium: mesh with Kelce as the rub/sit and Walker as the outlet; do not live on 47 dropbacks again.
Defensively, start in a Cover-2 shell and make Miami drive the field; Bolton and the second level have to tackle in space instead of posting another 13-tackle chase.
On third-and-long, simulated pressure — show heat, drop an end, green-dog Bolton — rather than pinning FAU's ears back through a quad issue.

nextGame.label: Week 3 · Sun, Sep 27 · 12:00 PM CT
nextGame.note: First road game of 2026 and the 3-0 chase; a double-digit favorite still has to prove the Colts tape does not travel.

spotlight.title: Spagnuolo already called the 30-point night what it was
spotlight.body: The Chiefs are 2-0, and that is the only result that counts in the standings. It is not the only result on the film. Allowing 30 points, 329 yards, and 24 first downs is the Week 3 install, not a footnote.

spotlight.title: Miami is being sold as a trap for a reason
spotlight.body: Winless opponent, noon kick, double-digit road favorite. That is the exact shape of a sloppy 2-0 trip if Kansas City plays the spread instead of the Colts tape.

spotlight.title: Conner's ramp-up is the timing, not the eraser
spotlight.body: Chamarri Conner is easing back at the perfect moment for a road secondary. The coaching point is snap count and communication, not asking a returning safety to cover for last week's 24 first downs.

spotlight.title: This 2-0 tape finally has more than one way to win
spotlight.body: Denver was the run. Indianapolis was the pass on top of the run. That is the version of Bieniemy's offense that can survive a South Florida noon kick — if they still hand Walker the ball 20-plus times.

spotlight.title: Rice's big play was a Week 1 leftover
spotlight.body: The first 20-plus against Indianapolis was not improvised. It was a look the Colts had already seen. Miami will see the same stems from Rice and Worthy if the run fake is real.

spotlight.title: Nohl Williams is playing like the next problem for opposing coordinators
spotlight.body: Through two games he is outplaying the corners drafted ahead of him. A Cover-2 road plan that lets him tackle and squeeze rather than live on an island is how you protect a ramping safety.

matchups.unit: Chiefs pass game vs. Miami coverage
matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy
matchups.note: Mahomes just went 32-of-47 for 382 and three scores with Kelce at 9-101-1. If Miami loads for Walker, the intermediate and vertical answers are already on tape.

matchups.unit: Chiefs run game vs. Miami front
matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III, Bieniemy under-center identity
matchups.note: 24-117 after 220 in Week 1. Mahomes can already see the box respecting the run. That is the lever for boots, not a reason to abandon the downhill game on the road.

matchups.chiefs: Steve Spagnuolo, Nick Bolton, returning Conner
matchups.note: Kansas City's talent edge is real; the Colts tape (30 points, 24 first downs, Taylor's 24-yarder) is also real. This is a self-scout game as much as a matchup game.
Nine catches, 101 yards, a 13-yard touchdown. Mesh and boot leaks are the third-down fix for a 5-of-13 night.
Interior pressure is still the identity. FAU popping up with a quad argues for simulated pressure and dropped ends rather than a four-man pin-the-ears plan all afternoon.
Williams is playing at a high level; Conner is ramping. Two-deep and rally-to-tackle is the grown-up answer on the road, not an island-man dare.

xsandos.title: Walker downhill, first snap in Miami
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, opening script, 12 personnel under center on the road vs. Miami
xsandos.why: Walker just carried 24 times for 117 after 220 in Week 1, and Mahomes has already seen defenses step down to stop that tape. A noon road game against a winless Miami team is won by staying on schedule, not by throwing it 47 times again. Bieniemy's identity is the clock; 37:00 against Indianapolis is the standard you take on the plane.
xsandos.coaching: Zone steps, one cut, no bounce. Walker has to press the line of scrimmage so Miami's linebackers cannot cheat the boot. Tight end seals the play-side end; if the safety is walking down, that is information for the next call, not a reason to abort this one.

xsandos.title: Cash the loaded box
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 after a Walker inside-zone look, same personnel, hash toward Kelce
xsandos.why: Indianapolis had already gotten the message from the Denver run tape, and Mahomes could see it. Miami will too. Booting him off the fake turns Kelce into the easy read and keeps a 382-yard passer off a stationary spot in a road pocket. This is the complement that makes 20 Walker carries sustainable instead of stubborn.
xsandos.coaching: Sell the run at the mesh point. Blind-side tackle and the pulling path have to wall the edge so Mahomes can play full-speed to the perimeter. Kelce leaks; Rice holds the deep safety with a post. Do not peek the rush — play the first open window.

xsandos.title: Punish the Cover-3 sit
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-7, 11 personnel, Miami two-high rotating to three-deep after eating two runs
xsandos.why: Rice's first explosive against Indianapolis was set up on the Week 1 tape; Worthy is the vertical closer who already finished from the 1. A winless Miami team that tries to keep a lid on Mahomes will live in three-deep. Four verticals is how you make the hole in the middle the story instead of another 5-of-13 third-down night.
xsandos.coaching: Outside receivers run through the corners, no hitch. Kelce or the inside stem bends to the hash and sits in the seam if the Mike drops. Mahomes' eyes go deep middle first — that is the 20-plus, not the checkdown.

xsandos.title: Fix 5-of-13 without another 47 dropbacks
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5, 11 personnel, Miami showing man from the slot
xsandos.why: Kelce at 9-101-1 is the man-beater, and the Colts night died on third down even with 523 yards. On the road you cannot wait for the next explosive. Mesh puts two crossers on a collision course, gives Worthy or Royals a rub, and leaves Walker as the outlet if Miami's rush follows the Colts' heat.
xsandos.coaching: Timing is the rub, not the win-your-1-on-1 speech. Kelce has to come tight off the mesh and sit if the linebacker trails. Mahomes hits the first separation; if both crossers are covered, the back is the throw. No hero ball on 3rd-and-5 in Miami.

xsandos.title: Take away the shot, live with the drive
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, Miami 11 personnel, Chiefs protecting a lead or protecting a noon road start
xsandos.why: Thirty points and 24 first downs against Indianapolis is what happens when the defense chases. Conner is easing back, so this is not an island-man Sunday. Two deep, five under, Nohl Williams squeezing the boundary, Bolton rallying — that is how you make Miami drive the field instead of exploding it.
xsandos.coaching: Safeties split the posts, no late rotation into a one-high look unless the motion forces it. Williams and the corners have to funnel, not grab. Bolton's 13 tackles last week were a chase; this week they have to be downhill after the catch, not 15 yards past the sticks.

xsandos.title: Heat without pinning FAU's ears back
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-7, Miami empty or 11, Chiefs need a stop after the Colts' 5-of-12 kept them alive
xsandos.why: Felix Anudike-Uzomah popping up with a quad is not the week to live on a four-man edge rush. Spagnuolo's signature is show heat, drop a lineman, send the second level. Interior pressure from Chris Jones and a reminder that Omarr Norman-Lott exists, plus Bolton as the green-dog, is how you get off the field without asking a banged-up edge to win the down.
xsandos.coaching: Show five at the snap, drop the end into the hook, and let Jones wreck the protection from inside. Bolton only comes if the back stays in; if the back releases, he is the flat defender. Do not give Miami the same clean third-down looks Daniel Jones had in the red zone.

coaching.topic: Andy Reid vs. the noon trap
coaching.detail: Reid's job this week is tempo and script, not speechmaking. First road kick, double-digit favorite, winless opponent — the veteran answer is to stay in the run-boot language that produced 37:00 against Indianapolis.

coaching.topic: Eric Bieniemy has both answers. He should still pick the run first.
coaching.detail: The pass cashed (382, three scores). The run is what made it cash. Twenty-plus Walker carries is how Miami's safeties get caught in-between, and how a 5-of-13 third-down night does not repeat.

coaching.topic: Steve Spagnuolo's self-scout is the actual game plan
coaching.detail: He is not pretending 30 points, 329 yards, and 24 first downs were a finishing-luck problem. Two-deep structure and simulated pressure are the grown-up calls with Conner ramping and FAU on the quad report.

injuries.note: Thursday report had him easing back into the Week 3 plan; his return is timed for a road secondary that just spent Sunday night chasing 24 first downs.
FAU popped up on the Wednesday report with a quad, which argues for simulated pressure rather than a four-man edge plan all afternoon in Miami.

personnel.detail: Kansas City stayed unbeaten while missing key starters through two games. Getting Conner back for the first road Sunday is about communication and a simpler coverage menu, not a sudden island-man identity.

personnel.move: Nohl Williams as a feature corner
personnel.detail: Through two games he is outplaying corners drafted ahead of him. A Cover-2 road plan that lets him tackle and squeeze is the right use, especially with Conner still easing back.
A second-round defensive tackle from a year ago is the depth piece you remember on a week when the edge is dealing with a quad and Spagnuolo wants interior disruption without pinning ears back.

personnel.move: Walker still the feature, not the decoy
personnel.detail: 24 carries, 117 yards, after 220 in Week 1. The pass cashed because that volume stayed real. Miami is not the week you cut him over to 12 touches because Mahomes just threw for 382.
The Week 2 chunk was set up on the Week 1 tape. Keep him on vertical stems off the run fake so Miami cannot sit on Kelce and Walker.

strategies: Open under center and hand it to Walker until Miami's safeties walk down — then boot Mahomes to Kelce.
Treat third down as an install, not a hope: mesh vs. man, easy outlets, no 47-dropback sequel.
Start the defense in a Cover-2 shell and make Miami drive; do not chase explosives after a 30-point night.
Use zone blitz and interior pressure so FAU's quad does not dictate a four-man rush plan.
Keep Conner's snap count honest: simpler two-deep rules, Williams on the boundary, Bolton rallying.
Win the noon clock. 37:00 against Indianapolis is the road standard; a track meet is Miami's only real path.
debates: Is Miami actually a trap, or is that just what 2-0 teams tell themselves before a noon road kick?
After 382 passing yards, how many Walker carries is 'respecting the identity' versus stubbornness?
Does Conner easing back mean a simpler coverage menu, or do you still ask this secondary to match Miami's speed?
Is 3-0 in September a real mark, or just the next sample size for a 7.6 percent Super Bowl ticket?
Should the Tyreek Hill reunion noise even be in the building this week, or is that a Wednesday story for a different roster?

runOfShow.talkTrack: Two-and-oh. 523 yards. Zero turnovers. And a defense that already said 30 was too many. Miami is not a bye.
Walk through the Colts tape: Walker 24-117, Mahomes 32-of-47 for 382 and three scores, Kelce 9-101-1, Bolton's 13 tackles as a warning, 5-of-13 on third down, overtime 33-30.
Complete offense, incomplete defensive standard. 3-0 chase, Raiders also unbeaten in the West, Polymarket still at 7.6 percent. Trap-game talk is real because the spread is real.
Conner easing back, FAU with a quad, Williams playing like a feature corner, Norman-Lott as interior insurance. No invented statuses — just what the reports actually said.
First road Sunday, noon CBS, five straight in the series. Run-boot script, mesh on third down, Cover-2 and zone blitz. Play the Colts tape, not the 10.5.
Six calls: inside zone, play-action boot, four verts, mesh, Cover-2, zone blitz — each tied to Walker, Kelce, Rice, Conner, FAU, and Spagnuolo's self-scout.
ESPN FPI 85.3 percent, DraftKings -10.5 on 45.5, Polymarket 7.6 percent to win it all and 16.5 percent in the AFC. Favorite on Sunday, sample size for January. See you at noon.
